en: In the diagram of the three realms,
the formless realm consists of ignorance, conceit, and craving, which are abandoned through cultivation.
[The objects of] ignorance, pride, greed, doubt, the view of precepts and observances, the grasping at views, false views, the path, ignorance,
pride, greed, doubt, the grasping at views, false views, cessation, ignorance, pride, greed, doubt, the grasping at views, false views, origination, ignorance, pride, greed, doubt,
the view of precepts and observances, the view of extremes, the view of self-identity, suffering, the form realm, ignorance, pride, greed, and cultivation— ignorance, pride, greed, and doubt.
The fetters of attachment to precepts and observances, views, grasping at views, wrong view, the path, ignorance, pride, greed, doubt, grasping at views, wrong view,
cessation, ignorance, pride, greed, doubt, grasping at views, wrong view, origination, ignorance, pride, greed, doubt, attachment to precepts and observances, wrong view, extreme view, and self-view;
and the fetters of desire for the realm of suffering, ignorance, pride, hatred, greed, cultivation, ignorance, pride, hatred, greed, doubt, and attachment to precepts and observances.
The afflictions abandoned through insight into the Path of Wrong View—namely ignorance, pride, hatred, greed, doubt, adherence to views, wrong view, and adherence to precepts and observances;

the afflictions abandoned through insight into the Cessation of Wrong View—namely ignorance, pride, hatred, greed, doubt, adherence to views, wrong view, and adherence to precepts and observances; the afflictions abandoned through insight into the Origin of Wrong View—namely ignorance, pride, hatred, greed, doubt, adherence to precepts and observances, wrong view, adherence to extreme views, and the view of self-identity—consist of thirty-two afflictions of the Desire Realm to be abandoned by insight into suffering. There are four [afflictions] to be abandoned through cultivation.
In the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), there are twenty-eight [defilements] abandoned through seeing and three abandoned through cultivation;
the same applies to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*).
Taken together across the three realms, there are ninety-eight.
This refers to the establishment of the names of the truths (*satya*) based on the distinctions of the sixteen aspects (*ākāra*) of those four truths.
As for the sixteen aspects,
they consist of the four aspects for each of the four truths.
The four aspects of the truth of suffering are impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self.
The four aspects of the truth of origination are cause, origination, production, and condition.
The four aspects of the truth of cessation are cessation, purity, excellence, and renunciation.
Regarding the four aspects of the Truth of the Path— path, method, practice, and deliverance—
the commentary states:
"Because it is subject to arising and ceasing, it is not permanent."
It is suffering because of its oppressive nature;
it is empty because it contradicts the view of "mine";
and it is non-self because it contradicts the view of "self."
It is the "cause" (hetu) because it can produce phenomena;
it is the "origination" (samudaya) because it is manifold;
it is the "arising" (jāti) because it constantly provides sustenance.
It is a condition because it assists each [skandha] individually;
it is cessation because all aggregates are exhausted;
it is purity because the three marks have subsided.
It is "sublime" because it is free from all afflictions;
it is "detached" because it is liberated from all calamities;
it is the "path" because its meaning is that of universal practice.
It is "Truth" (satya) because it accords with correct principle;
it is "Path" (mārga) because it correctly leads toward [liberation];
it is "Departure" (niḥsaraṇa) because it can transcend [suffering] forever.
Regarding the Truth of Suffering, there are four knowledges:
first, the patience regarding the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-kṣānti); second, the knowledge regarding the dharma of suffering (duḥkha-dharma-jñāna).
Third is the patience regarding the category of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-kṣānti); fourth is the subsequent knowledge regarding the category of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna).
These serve as the antidotes to the ten types of afflictions, such as the view of a self-identity (satkāya-dṛṣṭi).
The same applies to the remaining three truths:

the patience regarding the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-kṣānti), the knowledge regarding the dharma of origination (samudaya-dharma-jñāna), the subsequent patience regarding origination (samudaya-anvaya-kṣānti), and the subsequent knowledge regarding origination (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna).
These counteract the seven underlying tendencies, beginning with false view.

The patience regarding the dharma of cessation (*nirodhadharmakṣānti*), the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodhadharmajñāna*), the subsequent patience regarding cessation (*nirodhānvayakṣānti*), and the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna*) are the antidotes to the afflictions associated with the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*). The patience regarding the dharma of the path (*mārgadharmakṣānti*), the knowledge of the dharma of the path (*mārgadharmajñāna*), the subsequent patience regarding the path (*mārgānvayakṣānti*), and the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) [are the antidotes to the afflictions associated with the truth of the path].
Regarding the path-truth as the antidote for the afflictions to be abandoned through cultivation:
it consists of the respective subsequent patiences and subsequent knowledges with respect to each of the four truths.
These serve as antidotes to the four afflictions of the desire realm: greed, hatred, pride, and ignorance.
